Order 
This is second bail application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Section 439 of Cr.P.C.) for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.521/2024 dated 11.06.2024 registered at Police Station Bargawan District Singrauli for the offence punishable under Sections 366, 376, 376(2)(n) and 312 of IPC.
2.
Learned counsel for the applicants contends that previous application filed by the applicant was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 20.08.2024 in M.Cr.C No.33767/2024.
It is contended by the applicant that as per the allegations levelled by the prosecutrix, the facts is undisputed that the applicant and the prosecutrix were known to each other since childhood.
The applicant used to reside in neighborhood and as he was residing in the close vicinity, the prosecutrix and the applicant were acquainted with each other.
The prosecutrix developed relationship with the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12124 2 MCRC-44760-2024 present applicant.
They used to talk on telephone.

Thereafter, there were physical relationship also, as a result of physical relationship eventually, the prosecutrix conceived then, a settlement arrived between the families of the present applicant and the prosecutrix and, through notary a marriage was also solemnized on 06.12.2020.
As per prosecution, it was assured by the applicant family that a proper marriage as per rituals would be solemnized.

However, later on according to prosecution, the present applicant and the Ashish @ Arvind Panika vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105386496/
1 family declined to enter in the wedlock and thus the report in question has been lodged.

sentences.text: It is contended by the counsel for the applicant that the applicant is in custody since 06.11.2024.
Prosecutrix was a major woman.
The factum of previous relationship is apparent from the perusal of the record as of now.
Not a single prosecution witness has been examined which is evident from the order sheets which have been produced during the course of hearing.
It is thus contended by the counsel that the implication is unsustainable, the applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.

3. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent has opposed the prayer while submitting inter-alia that the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C directly indicates the commission of offence by the present applicant.
Hence, counsel submits that no case for grant of bail is made out.

4. Heard the submissions and perused the case diary.
5.

Thus, taking into consideration the totality of circumstances of the case including the fact that prosecutrix was a major woman and applicant and the prosecutrix were known to each other since childhood.

A settlement NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12124 3 MCRC-44760-2024 arrived between the families of the present applicant and the prosecutrix and, through notary a marriage was also solemnized on 06.12.2020, this Court is of the considered view that it is a fit case to release the applicant on bail.
Therefore, without expressing any view on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

6. It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during the pendency of trial.

7. It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 480(3) of the Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
8.
Accordingly, M.Cr.C. stands disposed of.
(MANINDER S. BHATTI) JUDGE Prar Ashish @ Arvind Panika vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105386496/
